input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party; provided that Corio or its Customer promptly notifies Commerce One in writing of any such claim and promptly tenders the control and the defense and settlement of any such claim to Commerce One at Commerce One's expense and with Commerce One's choice of counsel.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us (Corio) and our Customers a full defend-and-indemnify from Commerce One for third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control, cooperation at Vendor's expense, right to join with own counsel) and the usual remedy ladder (procure rights, replace/modify, or terminate with pro-rated refund). The Section 8.2 carve-outs are the customary ones (use outside the Documentation; third-party modification) and are narrower than the fallback's permitted exclusions. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity for the Vendor's software, so the walk-away scenario (one-way Customer indemnity) does not arise. Section 9 expressly excludes "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" from both the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages waiver, so the Vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. The clause therefore satisfies the fallback and substantially the preferred position on IP. Noted but not flagged: the indemnity does not extend to Vendor's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to Corio data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, which are preferred-position add-ons rather than material failures of the fallback.
